The 5 stories below are editorially right but 4 of 5 are short-WEB-only in the current corpus (1121 Hannah, 1448 David cave, 1477 Job 19, 1177 Simeon). _documentation._arcShape: Five pillars of waiting, one story each: longing → danger → suffering → promise → fulfillment.
_documentation._themeWord: Waiting (or 'waiting on God'). This is the theme-word that the compositional offer line would name. Per Slice 2 audio pattern B, this would be a new clip family — 'theme-word clips' — rendered per voice, parallel to the name clips Slice 2d already renders. For Slice 2 first ship, render one such clip per voice for this journey: 'waiting on God' or similar. Adam to confirm the exact phrasing before audio render.
_documentation._releaseGate: Loader MUST exclude journeys where status != 'ready'. Held journeys are editorial artifacts visible to curators, never loaded at runtime.

editorialNote: Five pillars of waiting, one story each. Each story is the canonical telling of its beat — no padding, no alternates. Spans Hebrew Bible (Hannah, David, Job, Isaiah) and New Testament (Simeon) to make the theme feel like Scripture's larger rhythm, not one tradition's idea.

stories.label: 1 Samuel 1:9-20 — Hannah prays for a son (waiting from longing)
stories.editorialNote: Chose 1121 (the ACT of waiting prayer) over 1169 (1 Sam 1:21-28, hannah_dedicates_samuel — the after-the-fact dedication). The journey's first beat is the prayer itself, the long ache before the answer.

stories.label: 1 Samuel 22:1-2 — David in the cave of Adullam (waiting in danger)
stories.editorialNote: Cleanest 'cave' story in the corpus — David's first cave, the four hundred gathering to him. Other David-cave moments (sparing Saul at En-gedi etc.) are about RESTRAINT, not waiting. 1448 is the waiting beat.

stories.label: Job 19:23-27 — 'I know that my Redeemer liveth' (waiting in suffering)
stories.editorialNote: Picked over 1055 (Job 1, trial begins) / 1153 (Job 38, whirlwind) / 1068/1076 (Job 42, restored). 1477 is Job DECLARING HOPE mid-wait — the wait expressing itself, not the wait beginning or ending. The theme demands the middle. Alternates: 1153 (Job 38 — God's answer after the wait) would also work as the third beat if you'd rather show the wait ending in encounter rather than declaration.

stories.label: Isaiah 40:12-31 — 'they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength' (the theological core)
stories.editorialNote: Picked over 1071/1079/806 (Isaiah 40:28-31, wings_like_eagles — narrower scope) and 1152/1500 (Isaiah 40:1-11, comfort_my_people — different opening). 1230 covers the broader Isaiah 40 wait theology and includes the literal 'wait upon the Lord' phrase. This is the theological hinge of the entire journey.

stories.label: Luke 2:25-38 — Simeon and Anna meet baby Jesus (waiting fulfilled)
stories.editorialNote: Only telling. The Christological closing of the wait theme — a lifetime of waiting met at the temple. Beautifully natural endpoint for the arc.

_excludedFromArcWithRationale: 1169 (1 Sam 1:21-28, hannah_dedicates_samuel) — after-the-fact dedication, not the wait itself
1133, 1496 (Hannah's song, 1 Sam 2:1-10) — celebration after the wait; arc ends with Simeon for tonal Christological close, not return to Hannah
1112, 826 (1 Sam 17, David vs Goliath) — about courage, not waiting
1022, 1030 (1 Sam 16:1-13, david_anointed) — also a 'long wait until reign' story, but the cave is the lived waiting; anointing is the seed
1052, 1060 (1 Sam 18:1-4, David & Jonathan) — friendship, not waiting
1055, 1063 (Job 1:1-22, tested) — the trial BEGINS; not the wait
1356 (Job 3, curses his birth) — the despair phase; could substitute for the middle Job beat if you want the darker register
1223 (Job 23, searches for God) — strong wait expression, alternate candidate for the Job beat
1153, 1530 (Job 38, whirlwind) — God's answer; wait ENDED. Strong alternate if you'd rather the third beat show resolution
1068, 1076 (Job 42, restored) — restoration; the wait's reward, but tonally heavy for the arc's middle
1071, 1079, 806 (Isaiah 40:28-31, wings_like_eagles) — narrower than 1230; if you'd rather the more famous 'wings' verses, swap
1152, 1500 (Isaiah 40:1-11, comfort) — different opening of Isaiah 40; less explicitly about waiting
1023, 1031 (Exodus 16, manna) — daily provision while waiting in wilderness. Could add as a sixth beat if you want a wilderness-provision pillar; held for tightness
1346, 1439 (Jonathan stories, 1 Sam 14) — adjacent material from the same era, not about waiting
1155, 1165, 1508, 1522 (Saul / Samuel stories) — same era, not the theme
